title: A separated finite-type scheme of dimension at most one has an ample invertible sheaf
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] whose structure morphism is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with topological Krull dimension $\dim X\leq1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (the Krull dimension of the underlying topological space; $X=\varnothing$ allowed). Then there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] which is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Lemma 0A25 (varieties-lemma-dim-1-quasi-projective), proof: 'By Proposition 33.38.12 the scheme X has an ample invertible sheaf'; the cited input is Proposition 33.38.12, Tag 09NZ (varieties-proposition-dim-1-noetherian-separated-has-ample, varieties.tex line 8164)

proof.text: $X$ is a Noetherian scheme. The field $k$ is a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is a one-point space, quasi-compact, covered by the single affine open $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with Noetherian ring of sections, hence locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and Noetherian. As the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type, $X$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact) by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

source.place: Lemma 0A25 (varieties-lemma-dim-1-quasi-projective, line 9202) applies 09NZ, whose hypothesis is 'Noetherian'; the Noetherian property of X is Morphisms Lemma 01T6 (morphisms-lemma-finite-type-noetherian)

proof.text: $X$ is separated: its structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, so $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated by [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated].

source.place: Lemma 0A25 applies 09NZ, whose hypothesis is 'separated' (absolute); Schemes Lemmas 01KN and 01KU

proof.text: Let Z = X_red and i : Z → X be its canonical map. The reduction theorem supplies reducedness, a closed immersion, and surjectivity. A closed immersion has an embedding as its underlying map, so surjectivity makes this map a homeomorphism. Noetherianity of Z follows directly from finite type of i over Noetherian X; separatedness follows from the separated composite i ≫ f over the affine field spectrum. Mathlib IsHomeomorph.topologicalKrullDim_eq transfers the dimension bound.

source.place: Proposition 09NZ (varieties-proposition-dim-1-noetherian-separated-has-ample, line 8164), proof, first sentence: 'Let Z subset X be the reduction of X'

proof.text: By [lem-sc-reduced-dim-le-one-ample], applied to the Noetherian reduced separated scheme $Z$ with $\dim Z\le1$ (step 3), there is an ample invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal N$.

source.place: Proposition 09NZ (varieties-proposition-dim-1-noetherian-separated-has-ample, line 8164), proof, first sentence: 'By Lemma 09NX the scheme Z has an ample invertible sheaf'

proof.text: IsNoetherian X supplies the NoetherianSpace X instance required by PicardLift, without separately choosing a minimal closed subset. Apply lem-sc-pic-lift-closed-immersion-dim-le-one to the ample invertible N on Z to obtain invertible L on X and e : i* L ≅ N. The pullback is invertible by lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor. The new isomorphism-invariance lemma lem-sc-ample-iso transports ampleness of N to i* L.

source.place: Proposition 09NZ (varieties-proposition-dim-1-noetherian-separated-has-ample, line 8164), proof, second sentence: 'Thus by Lemma 09NY there exists an invertible O_X-module L on X whose restriction to Z is ample'

proof.text: $i:Z\to X$ is a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes (steps 1 and 3) which is a homeomorphism of $Z$ onto $X$ (step 3), and $i^*\mathcal L$ is ample on $Z$ (step 5). By [lem-sc-ample-on-reduction-noetherian], $\mathcal L$ is an ample invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module, which proves the statement.

source.place: Proposition 09NZ (varieties-proposition-dim-1-noetherian-separated-has-ample, line 8164), proof, third sentence: 'Then L is ample by an application of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MS'

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks 09NZ (varieties.tex line 8164) as applied in 0A25: X is Noetherian (01T6) and separated (01KN+01KU, new Mathlib leaf); its reduction Z is reduced, Noetherian, separated, homeomorphic to X (reduction node, closed immersion finite, finite over separated finite type); Z has an ample invertible module by 09NX (new node, stated for dim <= 1); 09NY (new node) lifts it to an invertible L on X with ample restriction; 09MS (new node) gives L ample. Statement: the dimension citation changed from def-pc-dimension (sup of dimensions of local rings, defined for nonempty X only) to def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, which is what the words 'topological Krull dimension' say (equal by lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings for nonempty X); the tag reference '01PS' dropped from the meaning, since def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module defines ampleness. Source gap: 09NZ, 09NX and 09ND are stated for dimension 1, while 0A25 uses 09NZ for dimension <= 1 and 09NX's proof applies 09ND to irreducible components that may be points; the new 09NX node is stated for dim <= 1 (an integral Noetherian scheme of dimension 0 is the spectrum of a field, affine, with O ample). No sorry-free slopmaster2 declaration states the item or a new node (slopmaster2's IsAmple is the relative very-ample-power notion on K-schemes and needs projectivity).
